entries.note: Kolkhof 2014 resolves (PMID 24621652); quote verbatim in abstract. Rat natriuresis numbers (0.3 mg/kg, 3-10x eplerenone) confirmed in FDA review primary pharmacology. Opening untested is right.

Quote verbatim (review Study 13786 reviewer comment). NCT01473108 has no posted results; CT.gov completion 2011-05-17, not 2010-11. readout_tier arguably downstream (urinary Na/K is physiology); descriptive only, decision 15.
Abstract quote verbatim. FDA review confirms 1 mg/kg minimum effective dose in the DOCA-salt/uninephrectomy rat and 'dose levels that induced natriuresis in animals'. Untested opening is right.

Quote verbatim. Table 22 confirmed: rat NOAEL 5/1.5 mg/kg, 308x/435x total, 6x/8x unbound at 20 mg; dog male 3x/2x. 'Largely saturated at 20 mg' confirmed. Margin comes from the GLP tox rat, not the DOCA-salt model; rule question.

Abstract quote verbatim. Review's primary pharmacology lists DOCA-salt UNx rat, SHRSP and chronic-MI rat only; zero hits for db/db, STZ, Zucker, ZSF1, cynomolgus. Arai 2016 is the same UNx DOCA/salt system; pooling is right.

JAMA abstract quote verbatim; primary is the day-90 UACR ratio; NCT01874431 results first posted 2021-05-04 confirmed. Paired, primary endpoint, same. ARTS-DN Japan (Katayama 2017, 10.1016/j.jdiacomp.2016.11.021) belongs in patient_trials.

NEJM abstract quote verbatim; epub 2020-10-23; NCT02540993 results 2021-07-19 and NCT02545049 2022-04-15 confirmed. ESAX-DN and apararenone quotes verbatim in their abstracts (apararenone epub 2020-09-24). Strengthening entry supported.

Bhuiyan 2019 resolves, epub 2019-01-21, quote verbatim. Opening untested stands, but the track should carry retrodiction: true (see entry 5); the group's 2020 KK-Ay paper names phase II/III UACR data as its motivation.

Retro right: KK-Ay mouse epub 2019-01-21, after ARTS-DN 2015. Quote verbatim. ESAX-DN topline was public in a 2019-11-07 Daiichi/Exelixis release (UACR remission 22.1% vs 4.0%), and phase 2b online 2019-06-27, so the year is 2019.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 6: status agreed (retro, decision on retrodiction); year is earliest public comparison, ESAX-DN topline 2019-11-07 (Exelixis/Daiichi release, Kidney Week abstract TH-PO1201, UACR remission 22.1% vs 4.0%), after the 2019-01 mouse, so 2019.

entries.note: Quote verbatim (IND received 2013-05-15). The electrolyte/adrenal toxicology sentence in confidence_note is verbatim in the review. IND-date proxy opening acceptable under decision 7.
Quote verbatim; 18% vs 9% confirmed in review; Agarwal 2022 (PMID 34732509) 21.4% vs 9.2% confirmed in abstract. Predicted potassium rise appeared; same.

Kolkhof 2014 abstract quote verbatim; equal heart/kidney autoradiographic distribution and 'reduced risk of electrolyte disturbances' are both in the abstract. Separate track from toxicology is defensible under decision 8.

Quote verbatim; the review's EPC section sets Kolkhof 2014 beside clinical data, so comparison_stated true holds. Only head-to-head is ARTS in HFrEF (Pitt 2013: lower hyperkalaemia vs spironolactone; 5.3/12.7% not in abstract); set imported_from to heart failure.
Arai 2015 resolves (PMID 26607463); 'with no hyperkalemia (>5.5mEq/L)' verbatim in abstract. Untested opening right; model_filed null is honest.

Quote verbatim. Contra defensible, but Ito 2020 abstract gives esaxerenone's own rate (K >=5.5/6.0 twice: 9% vs 2%), so src can be product-matched (product_in_model true); 'rate not in the abstract' is wrong. Rats lacked CKD/RAS blockade; rule question.
Snelder resolves (PMID 31583611, PMC7051931); conclusion quote verbatim. Crossref online 2019-10-04, print 2020-03, so year 2019 by rule 6. Untested opener; finerenone, oral, unselected hold.

Quote verbatim (review p.19-20, EC50 0.165 vs 32 ug/L; 'largely saturated at 20 mg' verbatim). Model online 2019-10, FIDELIO result 2020-10: prospective, same. margin_stated true fits 'tolerated dose at or above the effective one' but no ceiling named; rule question.

Full text PMC6189469: quote verbatim, received 2018-06-14. No Munich/MWF hit in the FDA review, model_filed false holds. Non-diabetic rat belongs: the relied-on DOCA-salt rat is also non-diabetic and the source compares with DKD patients.

Quote verbatim (discussion, Bakris 2015); introduction cites ARTS-DN dose-dependent albuminuria reductions, so post-dates and motivated by the patient result: retro. within_2x holds (>40% vs 35% table / 38% text in the review at 20 mg).

Abstract quote verbatim; epub 2023-10-11. Full text was scrapable (60 kB): at 6 weeks the diabetic group was not albuminuric above control, so the model lacks the class's albuminuria phenotype. Opening untested right.

Full text 3.3: 'UAE, urinary creatinine, UPCR, creatinine clearance and plasma creatinine ... no significant effect of FIN'. The only trial-mapped readout is null in a model without the phenotype; Kim-1/Ngal mRNA are mechanistic, the bar the draft used to not score Yang 2025. Fold into the opening.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 10 via decision 4: a retrodiction reproduces the human data on a trial-mapped readout; UAE/UPCR/CrCl/plasma creatinine null, Kim-1/Ngal mRNA map to no FIDELIO endpoint. Not contra: non-albuminuric model = untested conditions (#35/#72), class never relied on it (#73).

entries.note: Abstract quote verbatim; intro esaxerenone UACR sentence confirmed by scrape. Earlier member db/db use exists: finerenone, Cells 2025-02-26, doi 10.3390/cells14050337 (PMC11898422, OA), 'attenuated the kidney injuries in established DN in db/db mice'; swap the opener, year 2025 unchanged.

Li 2025 Cells resolves (PMID 40072066, 2025-02-26). Quote and the 'confirmed in DM and CKD patients' premise are verbatim. Post-FIDELIO, so retro. Hirohama 2021 is UNx-high-salt db/db, a separate system (see missing).

DOI resolves to Lima-Posada, Int J Mol Sci 2023 (PMID 36768859, first published 2023-01-28); abstract quote verbatim in MDPI full text. Finerenone 10 mg/kg/day x12 weeks in ZSF1 rats; untested opener at first member use, 2023, class level is right.

Discussion quote verbatim; Results: no impact on BUN, UACR, glomerular/tubular injury or fibrosis. Run after FIDELIO/FIGARO, which the intro cites, so retrodiction; failed reproduction is contra by the retrodiction rule. Comparison is to rodent models only, so comparison_stated false is right; src could name FIDELIO-DKD as the patient side.

Same Li 2025 abstract, quote verbatim, epub 2025-02-26. Untested opener for finerenone on plain db/db; finerenone, oral, unselected hold. Opener would move to 2021 only if Hirohama's UNx-HS db/db were pooled into this model_id.

Arai 2016 JPET resolves (PMID 27384074, epub 2016-07-06); quote verbatim. Untested opener for esaxerenone on the DOCA-salt rat; model_first_use_year 2014 is the shared model_id's value. Drug and route hold.

Retro right: rat 2016-07, after ARTS-DN 2015. ESAX-DN quote verbatim (epub 2020-11-25), but ESAX-DN topline release was 2019-11-07 and phase 2b met its UACR primary online 2019-06-27, so the year is 2019.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 6: status agreed (retro); ESAX-DN UACR remission 22.1% vs 4.0% was public 2019-11-07 (sponsor release and Kidney Week 2019 abstract) before the 2020 CJASN paper, so the entry dates 2019.

entries.note: Arai 2015 'no hyperkalemia (>5.5mEq/L)' and ESAX-DN 9% vs 2% are verbatim; contra, product-matched and prospective. The 2019-11-07 ESAX-DN release (hyperkalaemia 8.8% vs 2.2%) and phase 2b (2019-06-27, hyperkalemia dose proportional) date it 2019.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 6: status agreed (contra, opposite); ESAX-DN hyperkalaemia 8.8% vs 2.2% was public 2019-11-07 in the sponsor release and Kidney Week 2019 abstract, earlier than the 2020 paper, so year 2019.

missing: Apararenone's own model: aldosterone-infused uninephrectomised rat (primary aldosteronism model), more potent organ protection than eplerenone; Discovery of Apararenone (MT-3995), J Med Chem 2022, doi:10.1021/acs.jmedchem.2c00402 (PMID 35652647). A member drug's own model (decision 8) with no track; published after the phase 2 (2020), so retrodiction-timed unless an earlier source exists.

Munich Wistar Fromter rat (non-diabetic CKD/albuminuria model): finerenone 10 mg/kg lowered albuminuria >40%; Front Pharmacol 2018, doi:10.3389/fphar.2018.01131 (PMID 30356804). A prospective pre-FIDELIO system with an albuminuria prediction and no track.

Second KK-Ay paper on the kkay-hs-diabetic-mouse track: esaxerenone + olmesartan in KK-Ay mice, explicitly motivated by 'phase II and III studies' UACR data; Hypertens Res 2020, doi:10.1038/s41440-020-0495-0 (PMID 32616846), epub 2020-07-02, before ESAX-DN (2020-11-25). Supports the retrodiction reading of that track.

Retrodictions after the clinic: esaxerenone in db/db mice, Life Sci 2025, doi:10.1016/j.lfs.2025.124008 (PMID 41067301); finerenone in a type 1 diabetes model, Biomed Pharmacother 2023, doi:10.1016/j.biopha.2023.115661 (PMID 37832406); finerenone in diabetic mice, Biochem Pharmacol 2026, doi:10.1016/j.bcp.2026.118370 (PMID 42612878). Each is a new system run after FIDELIO/ESAX-DN and belongs on its own track with retrodiction: true (decision 10).

Patient datum omitted from efficacy patient_trials and relevant to the Dahl-rat contra dating: ARTS-DN Japan, n=96, nominally significant UACR reduction, 'no patients developed hyperkalemia'; Katayama 2017, J Diabetes Complications, doi:10.1016/j.jdiacomp.2016.11.021 (PMID 28025025), epub 2016-12-14.

Healthy conscious dog natriuresis (urinary Na+/K+ up at >=10 mg/kg) in the FDA integrated review primary pharmacology, a second species on the natriuresis engagement track; descriptive, changes no status.

ZSF1 obese hypertensive diabetic rat (standard T2D nephropathy model) with finerenone 10 mg/kg/day x12 weeks: UACR raised at baseline and 'Finerenone treatment did not impact kidney function but reduced renal hypertrophy'; Int J Mol Sci 2023, doi:10.3390/ijms24032536 (PMID 36768859, OA). Post-FIDELIO member use, HFpEF-framed: a retro-timed track whose kidney-function readout failed to reproduce (decision 10 contra candidate); no track and not in considered_not_added.

Not a new system, an earlier source for the dbdb-mouse track: finerenone in db/db mice, Cells 2025, doi:10.3390/cells14050337 (PMID 40072066, PMC11898422, OA, epub 2025-02-26), 'attenuated the kidney injuries in established DN in db/db mice' with the patient benefit stated as premise; precedes Yang 2025 (2025-10-09) and Wang 2026 as opener and as the retro source.

Hirohama 2021 (Hypertension, doi 10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.121.17263, epub 2021-06-01): finerenone ameliorated hypertension, albuminuria and glomerular injury in uninephrectomised high-salt db/db mice, post-FIDELIO; a finerenone UNx-HS db/db track (untested 2021, then retro vs FIDELIO-DKD) has none.
rule_questions: Decision 10 scope: when another member's trial (ARTS-DN, 2015) has already answered the class-level question, is a later member's own first disease model (KK-Ay mouse, 2019, before that member's phase 3) a retrodiction, or a fresh prospective prediction for that member?

Decision 16: may the stated tolerability margin come from a different system and track (GLP toxicology rat NOAEL) than the efficacy model whose regimen target is scored (DOCA-salt rat), and does a margin held in the IND but first public in the approval review count as 'stated before the trial'?

Decision 5 converse: a rat absence claim ('no hyperkalaemia') made in non-CKD animals without RAS blockade, against patients on maximal RAS blockade with eGFR 25-60: tested prediction (contra, opposite) or 'conditions the model never tested' (untested)? And is such a contra dated to the first patient dataset that could show the harm (ARTS-DN Japan 2016, n=96, none seen; esaxerenone phase 2b 2019) or the first adequately powered one (2020)?

Decision 15: is in-vivo blockade of an exogenous MR-agonist challenge (fludrocortisone natriuresis in healthy men) proximal, downstream, or the in-vivo analogue of 'ex-vivo blockade of a stimulus' (direct)?

Decision 10 readout floor (models run): when a post-clinic model's only trial-mapped readout (albuminuria, creatinine clearance) is null or unmeasured and only mechanistic markers move (Kim-1/Ngal mRNA, glomerular fibrosis histology, macrophage proliferation), is the entry retro, untested or contra? The draft scored Kim-1/Ngal and fibrosis but not macrophage proliferation.

Decision 8 scope and decision 16 (models run): is a population PK/exposure-response model fitted to the class's own phase 2b patient data a 'model system' (subjects patients, predicting patients), like in-silico QST? If so, does 'doses of both 10 and 20 mg appear safe' from simulated potassium/eGFR count as a stated margin when the source names no ceiling dose?

Decision 8 pooling versus 'a member drug's own model' (models run): does apararenone's aldosterone-infused uninephrectomised rat share the docasalt-unx-rat track (same mineralocorticoid-excess UNx injury, same prediction) or earn its own? And under decisions 7 and 10, is a discovery paper published after the clinic (J Med Chem 2022) describing work that preceded phase 1 a retrodiction, or a prospective model dated late? The pooled mention promised on efficacy index 1 was not added.

Decision 8 tile scope (models run): a non-diabetic albuminuric CKD rat (MWF) on a DKD tile, prediction_level class and no cross_indication flag, accepted because the class's relied-on DOCA-salt rat is also non-diabetic and the source compares with DKD patients; confirm the convention.
could_not_verify: ESAX-DN JAPIC registry id and full-text potassium tables: Europe PMC fullTextXML for PMC7769030 returned no content and the PubMed XML carries no databank id; abstract-level only.

ARTS (Pitt 2013) hyperkalaemia incidences 5.3% vs 12.7% cited in safety entry 4: not in the abstract; the abstract confirms smaller potassium increases and lower hyperkalaemia incidence versus spironolactone.
Esaxerenone phase 2b (Ito 2019, doi:10.2215/CJN.14751218, epub 2019-06-27) now resolves; its serum potassium data were not read, so the earlier-dating alternative for safety entry 6 is unchecked.
Kolkhof 2014, Arai 2015/2016, Bhuiyan 2019, Bakris 2015/2020, Ito 2020: paywalled, abstracts only.
